column1: # 50-recovery-v3-arity-contract.tsv
# Producer/consumer row-cardinality contract sweep across every mode of
# tools/run-v07-genomic-recovery-v3.sh in the R repo (hsquared), sealed at commit 5325e95.
# Purpose: name arity as DATA (an expression over the manifest/plan/disk state) instead of
# independent literals on the producer side and the consumer side -- the root cause of the
# D1 recovery-v3 RC=21 death (smoke-n-ladder emits |unique(manifest$n)|=4 attempt rows;
# recommend_workers() requires >=16 before it will compute a worker recommendation).
# This file is a DECLARATION for future implementation review only. It authorizes no
# campaign, no code change, and no re-run of D1; D1 remains paused per ROADMAP.md.
# Read via `git show 5325e95:<path>` only; the hsquared working tree was not checked out,
# not modified, and no seed space or protected state was touched while building this file.
# SCOPE FENCE (this file is often read in isolation -- the fence travels with it):
#   This satisfies exactly ONE of the six successor preconditions in
#   docs/dev-log/handover/2026-07-20-d1-reseal4-postdraw-retirement.md -- "launcher contract
#   investigation". The other FIVE remain OPEN: a new root; a disjoint allocation; a new
#   pre-registration; fresh mutation controls/reviews/preseal; and explicit authorization.
#   attempts_per_rung = 4 (where referenced downstream) is an OWNER DECISION of 2026-07-20,
#   NOT intent recovered from the retired controller or the failed campaign.
# CLAIM CEILING (unchanged by this file): public_covered_count=5; ordinary_auto_genomic held;
#   V2-GRM/V2-GINV partial; D1 paused and unadjudicated. No route, count, or capability moves.
mode
smoke-n-ladder
column2: WORKERS (optional, default 1; xargs -P parallelism -- NOT an attempt/row count; positive integer <=96 via require_workers)
column4: |unique(manifest$n)| (one row per first-seen distinct n; 4 for the D0F/D1 cell design with n in {120,300,600,1200})
column5: recommend_workers (R heredoc; invoked from a LATER mode -- run-official, recompute-base-r, replay-julia, or standalone recommend-workers -- never from smoke-n-ladder itself)
column7: require_workers; require_preseal_worker_cap; validate_d0f_predecessor_once; run_official_pairs materializes the piped rows into $out/attempts/$stage/<group>/<seed>.tsv; verify-phase runs after with require_complete=FALSE (does not itself gate row count)

column1: smoke-16
column2: WORKERS (optional, default 16; xargs -P parallelism -- coincidentally equal to the row-slice constant below, a second literal-16 collision hazard; NOT the row count)
column4: n_missing = count(manifest_pairs() rows where BOTH $out/attempts/$stage/<group>/<seed>.tsv AND its .tsv.sha256 sidecar are absent) -- PARTIAL-WRITE BLIND SPOT: a row with the .tsv present but its sidecar missing is silently NOT counted as missing (:380-387), unlike manifest_missing_recompute_pairs (:389-395) which routes via resumable_pair_state (:83-105) and DIES on exactly that partial condition
column6: predicate `(( count >= 16 ))` (at-least-16) but die message reads "smoke-16 requires exactly 16 previously missing rows" (implies ==16); bash then slices ${smoke_rows[@]:0:16} = min(16, n_missing) rows forward to run_official_pairs uncontested
column7: require_workers; require_preseal_worker_cap; validate_d0f_predecessor_once; guard-selftest (lines 169-170) exercises the >=16 boundary with a fabricated count=15 negative control but never checks the die message text -- the message drift is caught only by the R testthat suite (tests/testthat/test-v07-genomic-recovery-v3-launcher.R:320-324, pinned at 5325e95), not by the bash self-test

column1: run-official
column2: WORKERS (required; xargs -P parallelism; gated <= recommend_workers() output -- see the separate gate row below)
column4: nrow(manifest) (every group/seed row, unconditionally -- no filtering for rows already attempted)
column6: 0 (xargs -r is a no-op on empty input; no lower bound is asserted on the piped row count)
column7: require_workers; require_preseal_worker_cap; recommend_workers precondition (separate row); validate_d0f_predecessor_once; verify-phase after

column1: run-official
column2: same WORKERS arg reused as the ceiling checked against recommend_workers() output, not as a row count
column4: count(pre-existing files under $out/attempts/$stage/**/*.tsv, written by an earlier, unnamed invocation) -- not produced or bounded by anything in this mode's own body
column7: require_workers; require_preseal_worker_cap; the die at `(( workers <= recommended ))` fires only after recommend_workers has already succeeded internally

column1: recompute-base-r
column2: WORKERS (required; xargs -P parallelism; gated <= recommend_workers() output)
column4: count(pre-existing files under $out/attempts/$stage/**/*.tsv) -- same external-state read as row 4

column1: recompute-base-r
column2: same WORKERS arg, now used as: (a) xargs -P for run_base_r_batches, and (b) the divisor in batch_size=ceil(missing/workers) when the plan is first written
column4: missing = count(manifest rows lacking a base_r_recompute/$stage/<group>/<seed>.tsv[.sha256] pair); batch_size = ceil(missing / workers)
column6: unique(plan$batch_id) -- re-derived by awk directly from the plan file's own batch_id column, not asserted against workers or missing by an independent literal
column7: prepare_base_r_batch_plan requires missing>0 before writing a plan, and refuses to touch a partial/nonregular pre-existing plan pair (die "external base-R batch plan is partial or nonregular")

column1: replay-julia
column2: WORKERS (required; xargs -P parallelism; gated <= recommend_workers() output)
column4: count(pre-existing files under $out/attempts/$stage/**/*.tsv) -- same external-state read as rows 4-5

column1: replay-julia
column2: same WORKERS arg, now used as: (a) xargs -P for run_julia_batches, and (b) --batch-count passed to the external Julia write-batch-manifests mode
column3: manifest_missing_recompute_pairs(julia_replay) [feeds prepare_julia_batch_dir, which invokes Julia's write-batch-manifests mode once, only if the batch dir does not already exist]
column4: missing = count(manifest rows lacking a julia_replay/$stage/<group>/<seed>.tsv[.sha256] pair); Julia is asked to write --batch-count=workers manifest files (bash does not itself assert how many files Julia must write)
column5: validate_julia_batch_inventory (called immediately after directory creation; run_julia_batches independently recounts the same glob before dispatch)
column6: count(files matching $stage-batch-*-of-*.tsv) in [1,96], and entries==2*count (primary+sidecar) -- re-derived by `find` directly from disk, not asserted equal to the workers/batch-count argument
column7: external batch dir must not be a symlink; must contain no symlinked members; run_julia_batches re-counts the same glob independently before dispatch

column1: recommend-workers
column3: (none -- reads whatever is already on disk under $out/attempts/$stage from any earlier invocation of smoke-n-ladder, smoke-16, or run-official)
column7: none in this mode beyond recommend_workers's own internal checks (schema completeness, n-coverage vs manifest, finite positive RSS, valid preseal cap, readable /proc/meminfo)
column8: 1:recommend_workers(count>=16; schema; n-coverage; RSS finite/positive; preseal-cap valid; /proc/meminfo readable)
